# #159 — Verify #147 identity/key model is enforced live (server + rtech-mcps + mcp2cli)

## Goal

Verify the #147 identity/key model is actually ENFORCED on the deployed server and reflected in downstream clients (rtech-mcps, mcp2cli), not just present in `main`. #147 was closed with the model defined in code; this issue proves it is live and tightly scoped before lane→shared-kb promotion is built on top of it.

## Why now

`src/namespace-policy.ts` references `openbrain-promoter` / `hermes-promoter` as the privileged shared-write identities (`:9-10`, `:55`), but `src/auth.ts` only mints roles `admin, agent, discord, n8n, readonly` (`:7-19`) — there is no distinct `*-promoter` role in the token map. So either promoter writes currently borrow `admin`/`n8n` rights (`namespace-policy.ts:59`), or the promoter identity is defined in policy but not issued as a scoped token. The live legacy promoter (PID 52082 on 10.71.1.21, per #145) is likely running as admin/n8n, not a tightly-scoped promoter token. That must be resolved before any new lane→shared-kb promotion path.

## Acceptance Criteria (live checks, no secret printing)

- [ ] Confirm how the running promoter authenticates today (which role/token). If it is `admin`/`n8n`, decide whether a dedicated `openbrain-promoter`/`hermes-promoter` token+role should be minted and wired into `auth.ts`.
- [ ] Live: Bilby/Skippy/Rico tokens can READ `shared-kb`.
- [ ] Live: a normal `agent` token is REJECTED when writing to `shared-kb` (prove the `:55` predicate fires).
- [ ] Live: the promoter identity CAN write `shared-kb` with provenance + audit receipt.
- [ ] rtech-mcps + mcp2cli reflect the correct tokens/roles (no agent carrying admin/promoter rights by accident).
- [ ] Docs confirm `shared-kb` is a namespace, not an identity, and the promoter role is the only shared-write path.

## Non-Goals
- No broad admin/promoter token distribution to normal agents.
- No secret printing.

## Relationship
- Closes the live-verification gap left by #147 (closed).
- **Blocks** the new lane→shared-kb promotion issue (promotion must run as a real promoter identity).
- Parallel to rtech-hermes#84 (Hermes write reliability, different repo).

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-06-19T14:09:52Z

## #159 audit results (code + live, read-only)

### Corrected premise
My earlier suspicion that shared-write rides on borrowed admin/n8n rights is **WRONG**. The enforcement is sound:
- `isPromoterIdentity` (`namespace-policy.ts:18-23`) requires role∈{admin,n8n} **AND** clientId∈{openbrain-promoter, hermes-promoter}. Bare admin/n8n tokens are **explicitly rejected** from shared-kb (test: `namespace-policy.test.ts:25-30`).
- Normal `agent` token rejected from shared-kb write (test: `namespace-policy.test.ts:31-34`); agents can read it (intended asymmetry).
- Enforcement centralized in `canWriteNamespace`, called by `promoteEntry` (`promotion-service.ts:121`). No security hole.

### The real gap: promoter identity is provisioning-dependent and NOT provisioned live
1. **Promoter is a clientId convention, not a first-class role.** It only exists if an operator provisions `AUTH_TOKEN_USER_OPENBRAIN_PROMOTER=n8n:<token>` (or hermes). No such wiring is committed in the repo.
2. **Live check on skippy-oc (`rico@10.71.1.21`): the promoter token is ABSENT.** Provisioned per-user tokens are `RICO, KEVIN, SKIPPY, GEETESH, LISA` — no `*_PROMOTER`. So the **token-gated promotion path is non-functional in production.**
3. **The live legacy promoter bypasses auth entirely.** Running process (PID 90680): `bun run scripts/promote-legacy-shared.ts --apply --loop --batch-size 250 --max-apply 100`. Per code (`promote-legacy-shared.ts:311-316`) it hardcodes a synthetic promoter `AuthInfo` and writes **directly to Postgres** — process-trust, not a credential, skipping the policy/audit request path. Fine for one-time local migration; NOT a foundation for ongoing agent-driven promotion.

### Impact on the pipeline
- **#161 (lane→shared-kb) is hard-blocked** until a real promoter token/identity is provisioned and the promotion runs over the authed request path, not a Postgres-direct bypass.
- **#160 (lane→own-durable) is unaffected** — within-namespace, no promoter gate.

### Acceptance-criteria status
- [x] Enforcement gate exists and is test-proven (code).

- [ ] **Promoter token provisioned live — FAILS (absent).**
- [ ] rtech-mcps/mcp2cli token review — pending (no agent should carry promoter clientId).
- [x] Docs: shared-kb is a namespace not an identity (confirmed in namespace-policy).

### Recommended next action
Decide between: (a) mint a real first-class `promoter` role in `auth.ts` + provision `AUTH_TOKEN_USER_*_PROMOTER` on hosts, vs (b) keep the clientId-on-n8n convention and just provision the per-user token. Either way the token must exist before #161. Health: server healthy, both workers OK.
